div.head: Leis Wl 28.2
div.ab: E si aveir trespasse par iloc u il deivent guaiter, e il ne puissent mustrer ne cri ne force que lur fust feite, si rendissent l’aveir.
Et si aveir trespassent per iloc u il de[iv]ent waiter, e il ne pussent mustrer ne cri ne force que lour fust faite, si rendisent l’aveir.
Quodsi aueria per locum custodie sue transducta fuerint, et non possint monstrare nec clamorem suum nec uim sibi illatam, reddent illa.
E si aveir trespasse par iloc u il deivent guaiter, e il ne puissent mustrer ne cri ne force que lur fust feite, si rendissent l'aveir.

28, 2. Und wenn Vieh dort, wo sie Wache halten sollen, widerrechtlich durchpassirt, ohne dass sie [ihr] Landgeschrei oder Gewalt, die ihnen [vom Treiber des geraubten Viehes] angethan wäre, nachweisen können, so sollen sie das Vieh [dem Verlierer] erstatten.

28, 2. And if cattle wrongfully pass through where they are to keep watch, without their being able to prove [their] hue and cry or violence that was done to them [by the driver of the stolen cattle], then they shall restore the cattle [to the loser].

And if livestock is taken over the stretch [of road] which it is their duty to watch, and they are unable to prove that they have raised an alarm or that force has been applied to them, they must pay compensation for the stock.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 266–267 (text and translation); Hk ends here (20–20.3a then follow in Hk, then ECf); from 29 Robertson's text is that of I.; Liebermann’s text and German translation added from Gesetze I p. 512–513, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

note.seg: in Hk folgt 20 bis 20, 3a [dann ohne Zwischenraum in derselben Hand E Cf.]; vielleicht im Orig. folgte 29 auf 20, 3a, als auch Bauern betreffend
in Hk 20 to 20, 3a follows [then, without a space and in the same hand, E Cf.]; perhaps in the original 29 followed 20, 3a, as likewise concerning peasants

Nicht ‘krepieren’ (Frühere) oder ‘von selbst, aufsichtslos durchgehen, fremdes Land betreten’ (Schmid) oder einfach ‘passer’ (Littré): dazu passt cri et force nicht. Trespass mit force ist Vergehen gegen Landfrieden; Pol Mai II 525; vgl. Gl Vieh 8b; Gerüfte 5

Not ‘perish’ (earlier writers) or ‘pass through of their own accord, unattended, and enter another’s land’ (Schmid) or simply ‘passer’ (Littré): cri et force does not fit these. Trespass with force is an offence against the public peace; Pol Mai II 525; cf. Gl Vieh 8b; Gerüfte 5
